A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRASP and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and appendices. Shared content can be matched across the substantial reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GRASP benchmark evaluations, compression and throughput measurements, calibration ablations and post-training convergence results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original GRASP benchmark, timing and sensitivity results in Sections 2–3 and the appendices. Its attribution of some baseline scores to prior work does not negate the original GRASP results.

M1.justification: v2 Eq. 6 ranks singular values using the signed score sigma_i times u_i^T G v_i. v3 Eq. 6 instead sums absolute parameter-gradient products over the singular value and both corresponding singular vectors. Algorithm 1 uses this group score, substantially changing the documented selection criterion. Cosine-based layer selection and the language-modeling objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 Table 2 adds substantial NLU/QA coverage, including CMNLI, CHID, C3, BoolQ, WSC, RACE-M/H, MMLU and CMMLU. Existing commonsense, GSM8K and LongBench coverage remains, with LongBench retained in Appendix A.6/Table 11. One added QA task has an unresolved naming discrepancy: the prose names CommonsenseQA, whereas Table 2 labels it CoQA.

E2.justification: LLM-Pruner enters the performance comparison, and LaCo and SliceGPT participate in the new post-training suite alongside ShortGPT and both LLM-Streamline variants. This replaces v2's dedicated four-model comparison against LoRA and the Streamline variants (Tables 2 and 10). The timing comparison also removes ASVD and adds LLM-Streamline (v2 Table 11 versus v3 Table 4).

E3.justification: v3 introduces OpenCompass accuracy evaluation in PPL mode for the added benchmark suite, using baseline scores attributed to Chen et al. GSM8K's stated setting changes from five-shot in v2 Appendix A.3 to zero-shot in v3 Section 3.2.3; this establishes a reported protocol revision, not that experiments were rerun. The new comparison's compression ratio is unresolved: Section 3.2.2 says 25%, but Table 2's caption says 20%.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted singular-value-group truncation sensitivity analysis examining whether magnitude predicts downstream importance (Section 2.2/Figure 2). It removes v2's post-training validation-loss analysis and curves (Appendix A.6/Figure 4). Calibration dataset/size and one-shot-versus-iterative pruning ablations are retained with unchanged values.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 Table 2 newly reports GRASP's 46.7 average accuracy and 94.9% retained performance on the added suite; Table 4 adds compensation times, including 0.66 hours for GRASP. LoRA/Streamline benchmark rows, numerous pruning-baseline perplexities, Table 3's perplexity column and peak-memory measurements disappear. Retained LongBench and ablation values are identical, as are Table 3's accuracy entries despite the stated GSM8K protocol change.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a formal singular-group importance definition and a second-order Taylor/Hessian expression leading to an absolute first-order approximation (Eqs. 3–6). This replaces v2's signed, singular-value-only perturbation formulation and changes the mathematical basis of importance estimation. The gradient-projection proof in Appendix A.1 is retained without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The central contribution of training-free gradient-guided compression with optional post-training recovery remains. v3 drops the abstract/conclusion's explicit perplexity-improvement emphasis, foregrounds low-rank replacement and accuracy/efficiency, and adds an explicit abstract claim of retaining 90% performance at 20% compression. These refine the claims without replacing the overall research contribution.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the explicit residual-stream/self-repair explanation with a low-rank redundancy account and acknowledges uncompensated GRASP's shortfall against SVD-LLM on LLaMA2-13B. Its limitations add failures of cosine-similarity heuristics and restrictions from needing gradients/internal access. Earlier domain-specific calibration and extreme-compression caveats are removed, while model-scale and language-coverage boundaries are restated more specifically.

D1.justification: v3 specifies A100-SXM4 80GB hardware and adds OpenCompass evaluation/access information. Resource disclosure changes from compression time plus peak memory to separate pruning and compensation times, and pseudocode no longer enumerates the exact attention/MLP weight matrices. The GRASP code link and detailed Alpaca/AdamW hyperparameter settings are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hua et al. (2025) and LeCun et al. (1989) for sensitivity/Taylor reasoning, plus LLM-Pruner and the new benchmark/evaluator references. It removes the Rushing–Nanda self-repair citation and condenses v2's three-part novelty contrast into gradient-guided low-rank positioning. Much of the existing compression-method discussion remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, discussion and limitations are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, experiments are reorganized into three numbered comparisons, and Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix into the main method section. Terminology shifts from representation evaluation/RLAL toward calibration and sensitivity.

P2.justification: The opening performance plot and full-width pipeline are replaced by a new overview, and a sensitivity figure is added. Cross-model results are additionally displayed as a bar chart, benchmark and resource tables are substantially restructured, and the calibration radar plot moves into the main text. Validation-loss curves disappear; the throughput plot and detailed LongBench table remain in new locations.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful NLU/QA evidence, a sensitivity analysis and more specific limitations. However, it removes convergence curves supporting its retained faster-recovery claim and several controlled baseline results. The revised scoring rule is not clearly connected to the numerically retained evaluations, while Table 2's compression ratio conflicts with the prose and GSM8K's stated protocol changes without changed scores. These evidential gains and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
